frontier.hypothesis: The entire remaining residual is one local-alloc decision: BB0's mask-value quantity (birth 6, death 10) must be seated at hard 4 instead of hard 3, which frees hard 3 for the blocks-0/1 address allocno and reproduces the target's whole block-0/1 register disposition.
frontier.mechanism: find_free_reg (local-alloc.c:2169-2247) scans hard regs numerically (no REG_ALLOC_ORDER on MIPS) over used = fixed_reg_set | regs_live_at[6..10) | ~GR_REGS. Hard 2 is excluded by the live call return $v0. To reach hard 4, hard 3 must ALSO be in regs_live_at over [6,10) at local-alloc time - which at that point can only come from another BB0 quantity that block_alloc ranked ahead of the mask value and that was itself seated at hard 3 with a span covering [6,10).
frontier.next_probe: Read block_alloc's qty ordering (qty_compare) in tools/gcc-2.7.2/local-alloc.c and enumerate what makes a BB0 quantity outrank the mask value; then spell, on the str1 chassis, C forms that create such a quantity WITHOUT re-ordering BB0 (x1/x2 failed because hoisting the p[8] read re-orders sched1).
